StahlKids.why_this_name: Both Stahl books were labelled with a shared 'Stahl ' prefix, so the model wrote bare 'Stahl p. 761' and no reader - human or code - could tell which of the two was meant. These names share no separable prefix, so 'Stahl' alone is never a valid citation label and is detectable as an error on sight.

Kaplan & Sadock Synopsis.note: NOT attached as a book. The examiners' required-literature list (P024-2026) names 14 Synopsis chapters that Dulcan under-covers, and each is cut into its own PDF under schedule/synopsis_slices/ (31-257 pages, all under 4MB, gitignored — regenerate with scripts/build_synopsis_slices.py). A chapter gets ONLY the slices mapped to it in that manifest, attached from disk, so the notebook holds the material the chapter must cite instead of 3,768 pages of mostly adult psychiatry. It stays listed here, and enabled, because books_directive() names the sources in the prompt and carries the rule that the Synopsis is cited BY CHAPTER — this edition has no printed folios (0 of 7 sampled pages). Drop it from this file and a chapter with a slice attached would be told nothing about how to cite it. Superseded: whole-book attachment (indexing `error` at 3,768 pages) and the three equal thirds that replaced it (seams mid-sentence, whole book in every notebook).
